topic: Continuous Batching Spikes Inference Tail Latencies
postText:
Maxing GPU utilization looks pristine on Grafana dashboards.
Until a 200ms real-time clinical alert halts behind a 4,000-token record summarization.

Modern serving engines rely on continuous batching and iteration-level scheduling to maximize throughput. Every generation step dynamically inserts new requests into active compute passes. But when mixed workloads hit identical model replicas, long-generation jobs monopolize iteration slots. GPU tensor cores run at 98% saturation, while P99 latency spikes out of control.

In healthcare IT systems where I work, mixing diagnostic classifiers and generative pipelines on shared GPU instances caused critical delays. Diagnostic endpoints must return deterministic responses within tight deadlines. Waiting for multi-second prompt prefills to clear decode loops destroys reliability.

Fixing this bottleneck requires defensive runtime design:
1. Workload Separation: Partition ingress traffic into latency-critical and throughput-tolerant pools with dedicated GPU clusters.
2. Chunked Prefills: Cap input chunk size so heavy prompts do not stall active decoding loops.
3. Priority Preemption: Evict speculative tokens and yield tensor cores immediately when high-priority tasks enter queue.

How do you handle noisy-neighbor isolation between interactive inference and heavy batch generation in production?
